title: Evaluating the Scalability and Adversarial Generalization of GRPO-Trained NLI Models
abstract: arXiv:2504.18376v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Natural Language Inference (NLI) is a central task in natural language understanding with applications in fact-checking, question answering, and information retrieval. Despite its importance, current NLI systems heavily rely on supervised learning with datasets that often contain annotation artifacts and biases, limiting generalization and real-world applicability. In this work, we apply a reinforcement learning-based approach using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for Chain-of-Thought (CoT) learning in NLI, eliminating the need for human-labeled rationales and enabling this type of training on challenging datasets such as ANLI. We fine-tune 7B, 14B, and 32B language models using parameter-efficient techniques (LoRA and QLoRA), demonstrating strong performance across standard and adversarial NLI benchmarks. translated_title: 评估GRPO训练的自然语言推理模型的可扩展性与对抗泛化能力
translated_abstract: 自然语言推理（NLI）是自然语言理解中的一项核心任务，在事实核查、问答和信息检索等领域有广泛应用。尽管其重要性显著，当前的NLI系统严重依赖于监督学习，而所使用的数据集往往包含标注伪影和偏差，限制了模型的泛化能力和现实世界的适用性。在这项工作中，我们采用基于强化学习的方法，使用组相对策略优化（GRPO）在NLI中进行思维链（CoT）学习，从而无需人工标注的推理依据，并使这种训练方式能够应用于ANLI等具有挑战性的数据集。我们使用参数高效技术（LoRA和QLoRA）对7B、14B和32B语言模型进行微调，在标准和对抗性NLI基准测试中均展现出强劲性能。在32B规模下，GRPO训练的模型在对抗性数据集上的泛化能力优于其他监督学习基线。
tldr: 该研究提出使用组相对策略优化（GRPO）进行自然语言推理的思维链强化学习，无需人工标注推理依据，并证明在32B模型规模下，GRPO训练的模型在对抗性基准上的泛化能力优于监督学习基线。
en_tdlr: This study applies Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for Chain-of-Thought learning in NLI without human-labeled rationales, demonstrating that GRPO-trained models at the 32B scale generalize better than supervised baselines on adversarial benchmarks.
